usage: I transfer to the subway here.
I must transfer at the next station.
examples: Please transfer to line 2 at City Hall station.
I transferred from the bus to the subway.
Where do I have to transfer?
nuance: 갈아타다 means changing from one vehicle to another, and the new vehicle takes the particle 로 or 으로.
mistakes: Do not forget the particle 로 on the vehicle you change to.

usage: I drive to work every day.
If you drink alcohol do not drive.
examples: Do not drive when you are tired.
nuance: 운전하다 means to operate a car, and the road or destination often takes the particle 에서 or 까지.
mistakes: Do not say 운전을 못 해요 split wrongly as 운전 못 을 해요.

usage: Do not park in front of the building.
examples: I parked in the underground parking lot.
nuance: 주차하다 means to leave a car in a spot, and the place where you park takes the particle 에.
mistakes: Do not confuse 주차하다 (park) with 운전하다 (drive).

usage: On weekends the roads are congested.
examples: The road was jammed because it was rush hour.
If you go now the road will be jammed.
오늘은 길이 안 막혀서 빨리 왔어요.
The road was clear today so I came quickly.
nuance: 막히다 describes a road being blocked or congested, and the road takes the subject particle 이 or 가.
mistakes: Do not use 막히다 for a person blocking the way.

usage: The child fell down on the street.
examples: I fell down on the icy road.
Do not run, you could fall.
Grandmother fell and went to the hospital.
nuance: 넘어지다 means a person loses balance and falls to the ground, often used with 에서 for the place.
mistakes: Do not confuse 넘어지다 (fall down) with 떨어지다 (drop or fall off).

usage: I bumped my head on the door.
examples: I ran in a hurry and bumped into the wall.
I bumped shoulders on the subway.
앞을 잘 보고 부딪치지 않게 조심하세요.
Look ahead and be careful not to bump into things.
nuance: 부딪치다 means to hit against something or someone, and the thing you hit takes the particle 에 or 와.
mistakes: Do not confuse 부딪치다 (bump into) with 만지다 (touch).

usage: The floor was wet so I slipped.
Do not slip on the snowy road.
examples: I slipped on the stairs and got hurt.
On rainy days you slip easily.
It is slippery so please walk slowly.
nuance: 미끄러지다 means to slide or lose footing on a slippery surface, and the place takes the particle 에서.
mistakes: Do not confuse 미끄러지다 (slip) with 넘어지다 (fall down).

usage: We have no time so let us hurry.
Take your time, do not hurry.
examples: I was late so I hurried a lot in the morning.
You must hurry so you do not miss the train.
If you hurry too much you make mistakes.
nuance: 서두르다 means to do something quickly because of limited time, and it is a 르 irregular verb.
mistakes: Do not write 서두러요; the correct present form is 서둘러요.

usage: I did not know the way so I wandered for a while.
If you look at a map you do not get lost.
examples: It was my first time in the area so I got lost a lot.
I did not know the address so I wandered the alleys.
I could not find the exit so I wandered in the station.
nuance: 헤매다 means to wander around without knowing the way, and the place you wander takes the particle 을 or 를.
mistakes: Do not confuse 헤매다 (wander) with 헤어지다 (break up).

usage: I stop by the mart after work.
Please stop by the post office on the way.
examples: I stopped by the pharmacy before going home.
If you come nearby please drop by my place.
I will stop by the bank for a moment.
nuance: 들르다 means to visit a place briefly on the way somewhere, and it is a ㅡ (으) irregular verb (the ㅡ drops, with no doubled ㄹ).
mistakes: Do not write 들르어요; the correct present form is 들러요.

usage: The road was jammed so I was late to work.
Do not be late tomorrow at all.
examples: I overslept so I was late to school.
If I miss the bus I will be late again.
If you leave early you are not late.
nuance: 지각하다 means to arrive late to school or work, and the place you arrive at takes the particle 에.
mistakes: Do not confuse 지각하다 (be late) with 늦다 (be late as adjective).

usage: I go meet my friend at the airport.
I will go to the station to meet you.
examples: My mother came to meet me at the station.
I have to go out to meet the guest.
Shall I go to the airport to meet you?
nuance: 마중하다 means to go out and greet an arriving person, and the person you meet takes the particle 을 or 를.
mistakes: Do not confuse 마중하다 (greet arrival) with 배웅하다 (see off).
